hints: Focus on what alkaline hydrolysis does, it splits the ester at the ester link to give a carboxylate salt plus an alcohol.
Work out the two parts of ethyl butanoate, the butanoate part comes from butanoic acid with 4 carbons and the ethyl part gives ethanol.
Match the sodium salt to the acid part of the ester, and remember the alcohol stays as a neutral molecule, not a sodium salt.
walkthrough:
**Write out what ethyl butanoate looks like**

Think of an ester as acid part + alcohol part joined together. Ethyl butanoate is made from butanoic acid and ethanol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Apply alkaline hydrolysis with NaOH**

With dilute NaOH, the ester bond breaks. The acid part becomes the sodium carboxylate salt, and the alcohol part becomes the free alcohol.

$$\text{ester} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{sodium carboxylate} + \text{alcohol}$$

**Identify the two products**

Here the acid part has 4 carbons, so you get sodium butanoate plus ethanol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Pick the listed product**

Sodium butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, is in the list, so that is the product to choose.

options.A: Correct. This is sodium butanoate, the sodium salt of butanoic acid. Alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl butanoate gives this salt plus ethanol, so this is a genuine product.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$ is sodium ethanoate with only 2 carbons. This would come from an ethyl ethanoate ester, not from a butanoate ester which has 4 carbons in the acid part.
options.C: Incorrect. The alcohol product is neutral ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, not sodium ethoxide. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{ONa}$ forms only when ethanol reacts with sodium metal, not in dilute aqueous NaOH hydrolysis.
options.D: Incorrect. Water is not formed here. Acid hydrolysis of an ester gives carboxylic acid plus alcohol, and alkaline hydrolysis gives carboxylate salt plus alcohol. Water is a reactant in acid hydrolysis, not a product of alkaline hydrolysis.
